info.title: Raven TUI RPC
info.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 contract between the Raven Python parent process (RpcServer) and the Node TUI child process (RpcClient). Single source of truth for both sides. Pydantic v2 models in raven/rpc/models.py and codegen-derived TypeScript types in ui-tui/src/rpc/generated.ts must stay in sync with this file. Drift is caught in CI by tests/test_rpc_schema_match.py and `npm run lint:rpc`.

methods.name: subagents.list
methods.summary: List every configured and preset-installable sub-agent as one overlay row set.

methods.name: subagents.add
methods.summary: Install a sub-agent from a preset into the running config. A cli or acp preset that would land enabled first has one real prompt sent through that agent, and the add is refused, reporting why, when it does not answer: that spends one call on the agent's own quota, can take up to 60s, and a refusal stores nothing at all. An openai preset and force: true are exempt.

methods.name: subagents.remove
methods.summary: Remove a configured sub-agent.

methods.name: subagents.build
methods.summary: Start building one vendored sub-agent's venv, and return as soon as it is under way.
methods.description: Not awaited, unlike every other method here: one of these is a few hundred MB of downloads, so holding the request open would time it out on the client and leave the build running with nobody able to see it. The row carries `building` until it finishes, which is what the page watches; success is read back off the filesystem rather than from the installer's exit status. Idempotent while running -- a second call for the same name reports the one already in flight rather than starting a second `uv sync` against the same directory.

building.description: True once the build is under way, including when one was already running.

detail.description: Why nothing new was started, or "" when this call started it.

methods.name: subagents.toggle
methods.summary: Enable or disable a configured sub-agent. Switching a cli or acp sub-agent on first sends one real prompt through that agent and refuses the enable, reporting why, when it does not answer: that spends one call on the agent's own quota and can take up to 60s. Switching off, an openai row and force: true are exempt.

methods.summary: Create one instance of an enabled, stateful sub-agent and switch to it.

schema.description: Which sub-agent to instantiate. Must be enabled and stateful: a direct chat is a continuation, and against a stateless agent every turn would start over.

methods.name: subagents.instance.forget

methods.name: subagents.instance.steer
methods.summary: Merge text into the turn one instance is running now. no_turn when nothing runs (nothing is started); unsupported when the run's transport cannot take text mid-turn.

methods.name: subagents.instance.set_mode
methods.summary: Report, set or clear the operating mode of one direct-chat instance. Neither field reports; clear=true drops the instance override, after which the session's tier (clamped to this agent's menu) is what the next dispatch runs at, and the agent's own default runs only where there is no tier to inherit; mode=<id> switches from the next turn on. Always answers with the override, what is inherited, and the whole menu, so one reply is enough to draw the control.

schema.description: Drop this instance's override, after which the session's tier is what the next dispatch runs at. mode wins when both are given: naming one is a statement, clearing is the absence of one. session.set_mode resolves the pair the other way, because there clear selects the configured default.

mode.description: This instance's own override, or null when it has none. Null is the ordinary answer to a read with no override set and to every clear, not an error.

inherited.description: What a dispatch runs at when there is no override: this session's tier, clamped to what the agent offers. Null when nothing is inherited and the agent's own default is what runs.

methods.name: session.set_mode
methods.summary: Report, set or clear the sub-agent tier this session dispatches at. Neither field reports; clear=true returns to the configured default; mode=<id> switches from the next turn on. Raven's own effort is the same in every tier.

schema.description: Drop the session override and go back to the configured default. Wins over mode when both are given, the opposite of subagents.instance.set_mode -- these are different operations: this one selects a tier, that one removes an override.

methods.name: reload.mcp
methods.summary: Reconcile the live MCP server set with the config on disk.
methods.description: MUST NOT throw. Today's only caller is the TUI's /reload-mcp, typed by a person; the method is also the seam a config-file watch would use, and such a caller fires on a timer, so a failure is reported as status='noop' with a message rather than as an error. Reloading moves the tool list, which is the first thing in the cached prompt prefix, so a caller that does not send confirm gets status='confirm_required' and nothing is reconnected. There is no 'and stop asking' flag: persisting that needs a settings section this config does not have.

methods.name: commands.catalog
methods.summary: Dynamic CLI command catalog reflected from the Typer app (replaces v0.0.2 -32012 stub).
methods.description: Reflects raven.cli.commands.app to build a slash-command catalog consumed by ui-tui's alias / prefix-1-match / multi-match-ambiguous logic in createSlashHandler.ts. Filters out _DISPATCH_BLACKLIST entries (gateway / provider login / channels login / sandbox shell / tui / onboard / upgrade / tracing compact) and agent-without-message. See harness-command-catalog-dynamic design.md §D1-D2.

BrowserRef.description: One actionable element, with the id a click can be aimed at.

value.description: Never present for a password field.

noop.description: True when nothing moved, including when the context engine owns compaction.

SessionInitInfo.description: The banner bundle: which model, which tools and skills, how full.

lazy.description: True when no agent loop was running, so tools/skills are empty.

tools.description: Tool names in a single 'builtin' bucket.

update_command.description: The command that would install the newer release.

config_notices.description: What a config migration changed on the user's behalf during this boot. Drained, so only the first session of a launch carries them.

endpoint.description: Which of a multi-endpoint provider's endpoints this session is on; null for single-endpoint ones.

title.description: The resumed session's name, when it has one. Absent on a fresh session, which has nothing to name yet. Carried on the bundle rather than fetched separately because a client resuming a session is already being told what it is resuming.

SessionUsage.description:
``info.usage`` — the boot baseline, refreshed by each turn's completion.

Distinct from :class:`TurnUsage`, which is the per-turn event payload:
this one carries the context-window fill a banner draws, and its counters
are named for the session rather than for one LLM call.

context_estimated.description: True when context_used is a tiktoken estimate of a resumed transcript, not a measurement.

TranscriptMessage.description: One stored message in wire form: ``content`` renamed to ``text``.

dag_run_id.description: The run a run_subagent_dag call started, so a resumed transcript can fetch its graph through dag.get. Absent on every other tool, and on a graph that was rejected before it ran.

spawn_task_id.description: The task id a spawn call's result names, so a resumed transcript can find the run's record through subagent.list. Absent on every other tool, and on a spawn that was refused before it ran.

reasoning_ms.description: How long the thought on this assistant entry took, measured server-side from the first reasoning delta to the first answer token or tool call. Absent means unknown (an unstreamed call, or a session written before it was recorded) -- render the bare header, never a zero.

duration_ms.description: How long the call this role='tool' entry answers ran, dispatch to result. Absent means unknown, same rule as reasoning_ms.

diff.description: A file tool's unified diff of the change it made, on its role='tool' entry.

origin.description: Present on the user entry of a turn the runtime opened, naming what opened it (`subagent`, `cron`, `sentinel`, `heartbeat`). Absent means a person typed it. Same rule as `notice`, one role over: the model reads `text`, a reader must not -- a sub-agent's announce carries an untrusted fence, an instance handle and an instruction not to repeat either to the user, and a cron reminder carries how to word the reply.

TranscriptDelegated.description: Which delegated run re-entered the conversation at this entry. The same identity `subagent.delivered` carries, so a replayed transcript and a live stream draw the same row from the same fields.

run_id.description: Set for kind=dag, so a client can open the run.

node_id.description: Set for a dag node's own message, so a client can place it against that row.

TranscriptNotice.description: Marks an assistant entry the runtime wrote rather than the model.

kind.description: Which runtime decision this reports; `action_blocked` today.

TranscriptTurnEnded.description: Why a turn's transcript stops where it does.

arguments.description: JSON-encoded arguments; re-serialized when stored as an object.

hub.description: Installed from the skill hub, so skillhub.remove can uninstall it.

mcp_server.description: Owning MCP server, or null for a built-in tool.

needs.description: Set when the tool exists but is withheld for want of a key. The model cannot call it; the row is here so the page can offer the field instead of the tool simply being absent.

setting.description: Dotted config key that unlocks the tool.

model.description: Empty when the shipped placeholder is still in place.

api_key_set.description: Whether a key is stored; the value never goes on the wire.

set.description: Whether a value is stored; the value itself never rides the wire.

fields.description: Every field the channel takes, so a client can render its configure form.

running.description: Whether the adapter is up, read from the live gateway. Null when no gateway answered.

connected.description: Whether the account is paired. Only the QR-login channels report this; null means the channel does not report a pairing and must not be drawn as disconnected.

qr_login.description: Whether this channel signs in by scanning a code.

MemoryItem.description:
One row, projected card-sized. ``kind`` decides which optional fields
carry a value: the four memory types share only ``id`` and ``kind``.

PlughubCatalogItem.description: The card-sized projection of a catalogue entry.

transport.description: None when the entry contributes no MCP server.

kinds.description: Which contribution kinds the entry carries: mcp, skill, python.

McpSnapshot.description:
One server's live connection state, as `MCPConnectionManager` reports it.

Every mutating `plug.*` call answers with this, and the gateway broadcasts the
same shape as an `mcp.status` notification, so a client renders one state
machine rather than two.

auth_url.description: The authorization URL this server is parked on, when it is. Carried on the pull because the `oauth.pending` notification that also carries it is dropped when no client is attached, which is every connect started at assembly time.

PlugLedger.description: What the install actually landed, which is what uninstall replays.

pieces.description: One entry per landed piece: {kind: 'mcp', server} or {kind: 'skill', name, skillhub_id}.

installed_name.description: The local directory name when installed, else empty.

JsonValue.description: Recursive JSON value type. Implemented as an unconstrained object in JSON Schema; downstream Pydantic uses typing.Any.

SessionListItem.description: One row in the TUI session picker (gatewayTypes.ts SessionListItem).

preview.description: First user message, used as the untitled-session identity fallback.

last_message_preview.description: Latest non-empty user or assistant message text.

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp of the latest user or assistant message.

pinned.description: User pinned this session to the top of the picker.

parameters.description: JSON Schema for the tool's input arguments.

id.description: A spawn's call id, or '<run_id>/<node>' for a graph node. Opaque to a client: a spawn row opens through subagent.context and a dag row through dag.node, which is what kind is for.

kind.description: spawn | dag. Which delegation path made this, and so how it is opened.

run_id.description: dag rows only: the graph run this node belongs to.

node.description: dag rows only: the node's id inside that run.

label.description: What it was asked, in short.

status.description: run | ok | error | cancelled | queued | skipped. The last two only occur for graph nodes.

agent.description: The external agent that ran it, or null for a raven subagent.

instance.description: The handle sharing one stateful agent session, if any.

started_at.description: ISO 8601; the record stores epoch millis.

ended_at.description: Absent while it is still running.

message_count.description: What was asked, plus the answer once there is one.

tokens.description: Input plus output tokens this run spent. Null, not zero, when the transport that ran it cannot report usage -- the cli lane never can.

tool_call_count.description: How many tools it called. Null where the transport has no per-step visibility.

vendored.description: Discovered under the `agents/` product tree rather than written into config: one of the agent products that ship with this raven, materialized as a row on every table build. Like `builtin` it leaves `configured` false -- there is no config entry to delete, and removing it means removing its folder -- but unlike `builtin` it is a real subprocess with a command, so it is probed and it can be unready (a missing engine wheel leaves it listed and disabled). The wire name predates the tree's rename. Absent from a server that predates discovery.

building.description: Always false from this server: the fork-era venv build is gone with the venvs, and `subagents.build` answers that there is nothing to build. Kept for wire compatibility with clients that predate the product tree. Absent from a server that predates discovery.

stateful.description: Reusing a handle continues this agent's conversation rather than starting a fresh one (`agent_meta`). What makes a row direct-chattable at all: `chat` refuses a stateless agent, so a picker that offers one is offering a refusal. Absent from a server that predates this, which reads as 'not offered' rather than as an error.

builtin.description: A built-in agent: raven's own in-process loop, on the agent table whether or not config mentions it. Distinct from `configured`, which stays false for one -- not writing a row is how 'use the package's default' is spelled, so there is nothing to delete and no transport to connect. It takes no action at all: `subagents.toggle` answers `config_field_readonly` for it, because an unnamed spawn and a dag node with no sub-agent both dispatch to this row, so it cannot leave the roster. A client must not offer a switch, a test or a delete for it.

upgrade_to.description: The transport this entry's preset has since moved to, or null when it is current. A configured entry is never rewritten underneath the user, so the mismatch is shown instead.

protocols.description: Effective API protocol keyed by model id.

protocol_overrides.description: Explicit user protocol overrides keyed by model id.

model_labels.description: Keyed by the model id as it appears in `models`.

ModelLabel.description: How a model reads to a person. Absent for a model no catalogue knows -- one released since the bundled snapshot, or served by a local deployment -- in which case the id is all there is to show.

ProviderEndpointInfo.description: One of a provider section's several url/key groups. `label` is the idempotency key the write methods address an entry by.

DirectTarget.description: One sub-agent instance a turn is addressed to. Null means the main conversation.

InstanceRow.description: One sub-agent instance this session has used, verbatim from the instance registry apart from `resumable`. camelCase because the web RPC serves the same record unchanged. `runId` / `nodeId` name the DAG node an instance belongs to: set on a dag-node row, and on the ordinary row of a stateful node, which is what lets one invocation's two rows be reported as one.

resumable.description: Whether a conversation can be opened with this row. False for a dag-node row, whose handle names a node rather than a conversation, and for an agent whose backend is not stateful. Answered by the server because statefulness is a property of the agent's configured backend, which no front end can read off the row.

title.description: What this instance was asked, in one line: a spawn's task_summary, or a graph node's node_summary, or -- for an instance nobody dispatched, one the user made by hand -- the first line of the message that opened it, taken once so later messages do not rename it. Absent only for work that ran before any of those existed, or when that first message yielded nothing; a reader falls back to the handle.

runTitle.description: What the graph this instance belongs to was dispatched for. Absent, not empty, for an instance that came from no orchestration, so its presence is what says the row has a source.

DirectTurn.description: One row of one instance's conversation. Preferred source is the instance's own log, which is written turn by turn and holds what the run did on the way; a conversation with no log falls back to its record directories, where a turn is a pair of files.

call_id.description: How this turn is addressed, which depends on which lane wrote it. A spawn turn carries the node id the model chose, and subagent.context reads it. A DAG node turn carries <run_id>/<node_id>, which subagent.context rejects (it refuses any id containing a slash) -- open those through dag.node. A direct-chat turn keeps its minted call id. Still spelled call_id on the wire for every lane.

reasoning_content.description: The thought that preceded this turn, where the transport reports one.

tool_calls.description: What this turn called on the way, matched to a later role='tool' row by id.

tool_call_id.description: On a role='tool' row, the call it answers.

live.description: Set on a row from a turn still running, which no record holds yet. Such rows are a snapshot: the next read replaces them, and the record replaces them once the turn lands.

steer.description: Set on a user row that was a steer: words merged into a turn already running, not the prompt that opened one. A reader draws it inside the turn rather than as a new one.

interrupted.description: Set on a trailing user row whose turn died with its session: nothing is running now and no reply ever landed. A reader marks the question as interrupted rather than leaving it hanging.

stdout.description: Rich-rendered output with ANSI SGR sequences.

stderr.description: Error / warning output with ANSI SGR sequences.

error_code.description: Only present for timeout / not-dispatch-compatible cases (mirrors a JSON-RPC error code).

error.description: Human-readable explanation of why this method is not supported in v0.1.

hint.description: Optional hint to the user (e.g., 'Press Ctrl+C').

canon.description: alias (with leading /) -> canonical mapping. v0.1: alias = canonical 1:1 (no short aliases generated; TS-side prefix-1-match handles partials). Group + subcommand are space-separated (e.g. '/channels status'), not slash- or dot-separated.

pairs.description: Ordered (alias, canonical) tuples. TS-side createGatewayEventHandler.ts:198 gates on non-empty pairs; empty pairs degrades to slash.exec direct dispatch.

sub.description: group -> [subcommand]. Blacklisted entries (e.g. channels login) and agent-REPL are filtered out.

categories.description: Ordered category list: '(top-level)' first then alphabetical group names. Fully filtered groups (e.g. tui) do not appear.

skill_count.description: Total skill count from skill_forge store SQL count; 0 if DB missing (warning field then populated).

warning.description: Optional warning pushed to TUI activity strip (e.g. 'skill store not initialized').

TurnStartedEvent.description: A turn the runtime opened (a delegated result re-entering the conversation) has begun. `turn.send` owns `message.start`, and the spine suppresses it for these turns, so this event is the client's only live signal that a new turn started. It advances the client's live turn bookkeeping (the workspace record's turn number, which the artifact bar reads), enters the busy state, and -- when `delegated` is present -- carries the delivery identity AND the injected text, so the delivery row is drawn at the moment the result is actually visible (its turn started), not when it was submitted. A stored delegated user entry draws the same row on replay, which is what keeps the two views in step.

node_id.description: Which node of the run this is about. Present only on `kind: dag` with `status: exception`, where the report concerns one node rather than the whole run.

content.description: The text that re-entered the conversation, verbatim; a client shows the reader-facing part of it by keeping only what sits INSIDE the untrusted fence.

payload.description: `target` names the conversation this event belongs to; absent is the main agent.

content.description: The message that started the turn. Present so a client that did not send it can draw the question: the user entry reaches the transcript only at turn end.

PermissionReviewEvent.description: The smart-mode permission reviewer started or finished looking at one tool call. Presentational only: it lets a surface name the pause on the running tool row instead of showing an unexplained stall; decisions never depend on it.

NoticeEvent.description:
Prose the runtime wrote, not the model.

It must not arrive as `token.delta`: that buffer is the model's voice, so the text would render as the answer -- glued to whatever the model narrated just before it, carrying the answer's copy and branch actions, and stuck in English whatever language the turn was in.

kind.description: Which runtime decision this reports; `action_blocked` today.

detail.description: The blocking tool's own first line, when it gave one.

blocking.description: The call is a blocking interaction with no automatic deadline. A client that clocks the event stream for liveness must suspend that clock while it is in flight.

FileChange.description: One file a tool call wrote, as contents rather than as a rendering of them. Beside ToolCompleteEvent.diff rather than instead of it: a client that draws its own diff needs the text, and a unified diff cannot be turned back into the file.

path.description: Absolute path of the file that was written.

after.description: The file's full contents after the write.

before.description: The contents the write replaced. Absent when the file did not exist, so a client renders a creation differently from a rewrite; an empty string means the file existed and was empty.

ok.description: Whether the tool call succeeded, by the emit site's verdict.

diff.description: Unified diff of what the call changed on disk, when the tool could produce one.

duration_ms.description: How long the whole turn took, measured server-side from the moment the runner picked the turn up to the moment it returned. Sent so a live client does not have to time the turn with its own clock: a browser stopwatch starts when the events arrive rather than when the work did, and only exists while that page is open, so the same turn came out one number live and another after a reload. Absent means unknown, same rule as reasoning_ms -- fall back to timing it locally, never to zero.

turn_id.description: The turn this failure belongs to. Empty when the emitter did not know it; a consumer that correlates a request to a turn must not treat an empty value as its own.

SessionTitledEvent.description: The model named this session, reading the opening message alongside the turn that carried it. Conversation-scoped, and emitted only when the title actually changed -- a client can replace what it is showing without comparing. A front end that parks a placeholder where the title goes fills it in here instead of showing a truncated first line and rewriting it a moment later.

SessionNamingEndedEvent.description: The naming call for this session finished without publishing a title. The other half of `session.titled`: exactly one of the two follows a turn whose `turn.send` reported `naming: true`, so a client parking a placeholder where the title goes can stop waiting on either instead of waiting out a grace period. `reason` is for the log and the bug report rather than for the reader -- 'timeout' the call outran its budget, 'no_title' it came back with nothing usable (the model answered without calling the naming tool, or the provider failed and generate_title swallowed it, logging the cause at debug), 'error' the naming code itself raised, 'renamed' a person named the session while the call ran.

SubagentDeliveredEvent.description: A delegated run's result re-entered its conversation here. Emitted just after the result is submitted to the main loop, so a client can mark the seam where the sub-agent's answer came back. The turn it opens is submitted through the spine, which emits no `message.start`, so this event is the only live signal that it happened -- and a client REPLAYING the session later reads the same identity off the stored user entry's `delegated` field, which is what keeps the two views agreeing.

label.description: The spawn's display label, or the dag's run_id.

run_id.description: Set for kind=dag, so a client can open the run.

content.description: The text that re-entered the conversation, verbatim. A client shows the reader-facing part of it by keeping only what sits INSIDE the untrusted fence -- and a client replaying this turn later reads the same string from the stored entry's `text`, so one rule over one input keeps the live view and the reloaded one from disagreeing about what was delivered.

node_id.description: Set for a dag node's own message, so a client can place it against that row.

SubagentStatusEvent.description: One spawned run's lifecycle transition, as it happens. 'subagent.delivered' marks where a finished result re-entered the conversation; this event is the run itself moving -- queued, started, finished -- so a client can render live delegation without polling the disk-backed lists. Terminal transitions are not replayed: a client that reconnects reconciles against subagent.list instead.

task_id.description: The manager's short id for this run, stable across its lifecycle.

call_id.description: The node id subagent.context reads -- the model's own name for the task, shared with run_subagent_dag's node ids. Sent from 'running' onward: the id is settled before dispatch, but a pending run has written no record, and advertising an id whose read comes back empty would draw a transcript that does not exist yet.

tool_call_id.description: The spawn tool call that dispatched this run, when the host correlates the two. What lets a client pin the run onto the tool row that made it, the same way dag.run_started names its call.

instance.description: The addressable handle, when the caller named or minted one.

DagNodeStatus.description: Per-node status reported by the DAG runner. 'interrupted' never comes off the wire -- it is what a client infers for a node still called running when the run stopped reporting. 'exception' is a node that finished without accomplishing its task and is waiting on a decision; it is not terminal.

DagSnapshotNodeStatus.description: Per-node status in a run read back off disk. Unlike the event vocabulary this includes 'interrupted', which the server infers for a node the registry still calls running on a run nothing is executing. 'exception' is a node that finished without accomplishing its task and is waiting on a decision; it is not terminal.

node_summary.description: One line, for the user, on what this node was asked to do. Absent on a run that predates the field.

inputs.description: What this node was handed, per key: a literal string, {file: path}, or {node: id}. The other half of prompt_template -- a template's {{ inputs.k }} does not say where k came from.

DagRunSnapshot.description: One run rebuilt from its run dir. 'finalized' is false while it is still executing, in which case per-node state came from the instance registry overlay rather than a manifest.

task_summary.description: What the whole graph was dispatched for, in one line. Absent for a run written before the field existed. Per-node the equivalent is DagSnapshotNode.node_summary.

DagNodeDetail.description: One node's rendered prompt and the head of its output. Either text is absent when its file does not exist: a node that never ran has no prompt, a failed one no output.

status.description: This node's own last recorded status; null when the run has written no manifest yet.

error.description: Why the node failed. A failed node has no output, so without this it reads as unanswered.

DagRunStartedEvent.description: A run_subagent_dag call accepted a graph. Carries the whole topology so a client can lay the graph out before any node reports.

tool_call_id.description: The call this run belongs to. Absent on hosts that do not correlate progress with a tool row.

task_summary.description: What the whole graph was dispatched for, in one line. Absent for a run started before the field existed. Per-node the equivalent is the node's node_summary.

instance.description: Shared stateful handle. Nodes naming the same one run sequentially.

node_summary.description: One line, for the user, on what this node was asked to do. Absent on a run that predates the field.

DagRunReplannedEvent.description: A replan decision started a successor run for a node that could not proceed; replan_run_id names the new run.

DagNodeStalledEvent.description: A running node has shown no sign of life for quiet_ms. Information only: the node is still running and nothing about the run changed.

DagRunCompletedEvent.description: The run finished. Terminal node output text is deliberately absent -- it is already in the tool result.

MediaItem.description: One file the agent produced as part of its reply, by local path.

path.description: Absolute path of the file on the machine the agent runs on.

mime.description: MIME type as declared by the emit site. Today every producer declares application/octet-stream, so a client that needs the real type should sniff the extension rather than trust this.

kind.description: Coarse media class; "file" is the only value emitted today.

items.description: The files, in the order the turn produced them. Never empty: an event with nothing to deliver is not emitted.

TurnEvent.description: Discriminated union of turn streaming events. The 'type' field is the discriminator.

KnowledgeBase.description:
One base as the list view needs it.

``embedding_model`` and ``dimensions`` are the base's own, recorded when it
was created rather than read from today's config -- a base outlives a change
to what the operator has configured, and the page has to be able to show the
mismatch.

KnowledgeDocument.description:
One uploaded document and where its indexing got to.

``error`` is empty unless ``status`` is ``failed``; a row carries the reason
with it so a reader does not have to go looking for why nothing is
searchable.

KnowledgeHit.description:
One search hit. ``score`` is a similarity, so higher is nearer -- the
direction every caller already reads.

PlaybookNodeShape.description:
Just enough of one step to draw the graph: which step it is, and what it
waits for. The library page draws a concept diagram per card, and shipping
the prompts and per-node config the detail view needs would be the whole
library on page open.

PlaybookRow.description:
One playbook as the library list needs it. ``error`` is empty unless the
file would not parse, in which case it carries the reason and ``nodes`` is
empty -- one unreadable file in a directory of user-edited text must not
take the page down with it. ``disabled`` lives in config rather than in the
file, because the file is the distribution unit and the switch is local to
this machine.

PlaybookParam.description:
One runtime input. ``description`` is the sentence the caller is asked when
the value is missing, so a form built from this uses it as the label.

PlaybookNode.description:
One step, whole. ``subagent`` / ``node_summary`` / ``prompt_template`` may
be empty: those three are the fields an author may leave blank for the
caller to fill at run time. ``skills`` / ``mcps`` are three-state -- null
means the author said nothing, ``[]`` means the author wrote an empty list,
and a list names what to consider.

PlaybookDetail.description:
One whole playbook: its identity, its runtime inputs, and either the graph
(``mode: dag``) or the assembly guidance a model turns into one
(``mode: prompt``). ``path`` is the file this was read from.

``version`` is the spec format version the file declares, not a revision of
the playbook's content.

PlaybookMcpServer.description: One MCP server the playbook itself carries, as the file declares it. Carries every field the runtime reads to decide what the server is and whether it runs. `env` and `headers` are declarations rather than resolved values: a carried server references a credential through `{{ params.X }}` and the run supplies it, so nothing here is ever a secret's value, and `has_oauth_config` says only whether the file declares OAuth endpoints, never what they are.
